{"content": "Istanbul Airport (Turkish: İstanbul Havalimanı; IATA: IST, ICAO: LTFM) is the main international airport of Istanbul, Turkey's largest city, and one of the busiest airports in the world. It is operated by iGA Airport Operation (iGA).

The airport is located in the Arnavutköy district of Istanbul, near the Black Sea coast, about 35 km (22 mi) northwest of the city center. The airport covers an area of 76.5 km2 (29.5 sq mi).

History


Construction
The idea of building a new airport in Istanbul was first suggested in 2003. After several years of feasibility studies, in 2013 the Turkish government initiated a competitive tender for the development, design, construction, operation, and transfer of the new airport. The tender was won by a consortium of five Turkish companies: Cengiz, Mapa, Limak, Kolin, and Kalyon, collectively known as "CCC (Cengiz, Kalyon, Kolin) + LimakMapa". The tender was won with a bid of 22.1 billion euros in fixed concession fees plus a variable component based on passenger numbers and retail revenue. The concession period is 25 years.

Opening
The airport was inaugurated on October 29, 2018, to coincide with the 95th anniversary of the Republic of Turkey. Full operations started on April 6, 2019, with the closure of the previous Atatürk Airport.


Terminals
Istanbul Airport has one terminal building and several concourses. The terminal building is the largest in the world under a single roof, covering an area of 1.4 million m2 (15 million sq ft), and can handle up to 90 million passengers per year. With six concourses (A, B, C, D, F and G), there are 143 contact gates.

Airport master plan

In 2022, construction started on the airport's second runway system. The airport currently has three parallel runways, with a fourth and fifth runway under construction. A sixth runway is planned for the future. When completed, the airport will have six runways in three parallel pairs. The airport is planned to eventually have a capacity of 200 million passengers per year.


Ground transportation

Metro
The M11 Istanbul Airport Metro opened on January 21, 2023, connecting the airport to the city center in 38 minutes, and has been operational since then. There are 20 stations on the line between Gayrettepe and Istanbul Airport.


Bus
HAVAŞ, the company that operates the airport bus service, provides frequent bus service from the airport to several destinations in Istanbul including Taksim Square, Kadıköy, Beşiktaş, Şişli, Mecidiyeköy, and Yenibosna.


Taxi
Taxis operate from a taxi rank on the arrivals level of the terminal building.


Car rental
Several international and domestic car rental companies operate from the airport.


Accommodation
The Istanbul Airport Hotel, a Yotel property, is located within the terminal building.
